guard: closing a run out of band from the record stream publishes ONE terminal — RUN_FINISHED, or RUN_ERROR when the connector reports a failed turn — consumes no source record, and refuses every state where publishing would be a guess
why: The plane reads a file and a harness reports the end of a turn through a lifecycle hook that
writes no record, so a hook-sourced terminal had no vehicle into a record-sourced stream. The
terminal added here is an ordinary frame with one exception, the source cursor, and that
exception is the whole risk: a closing frame that advanced the cursor would mark records
consumed that were never mapped, and a consumer would see no seq gap to notice it by.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, checked rather than assumed. The suite imports the emitter and the holder
by RELATIVE SOURCE PATH (../src/agui.js, ../src/agui-holder.js), so the bytes mutated are the
bytes graded. There is no dist in the path and no build in the command. Its one package-name
import is `type Part` from @cotal-ai/core, which is erased at compile time and carries no
behaviour.
NOT PROVED HERE, named rather than implied. The clone validation before the publish carries no
kill: a closing unit is one event and the real bracket machine refuses it before mutating, so
removing the clone changes nothing observable. It is symmetry with `pump`, where a multi-event
batch makes it load-bearing. And the holder cell about starting nothing is enforced by a
signature that takes no path, so it is a fence against a future signature rather than evidence
about this one.
K6 and K7 are the error close, and they are two mutations rather than one because the failure
travels through two objects: the emitter decides WHICH terminal to build, and the holder decides
whether the reason it was handed reaches the emitter at all. A connector that reports a failed
turn to a holder that drops it on the floor publishes a finish, and that is indistinguishable on
the wire from never having reported it.
K8 is the size bound on that same close. An oversized upstream detail used to make packUnits
refuse before beginSend, so the run got no terminal and the holder died. The bound is one call
on the shared close; skipping it restores the defect.
K9 is the never-both-terminal property. Deleting this.run = undefined from the shared terminal
arm of AguiBrackets.accept leaves the machine open, so a second close publishes a finish. The
earlier claim that no such deletion existed was false; the cell already graded the property.

mutations.name: K1 the closing frame takes its cursor from a fresh source read, the copy-paste from pump
mutations.note: The plausible authoring error, not a contrived one: pump ends by advancing to the read end, and repeating that here swallows any record that landed between the flush and the close.

mutations.name: K2 mint a run id when none is open instead of answering null
mutations.find:
const runId = this.brackets.runId;
    if (runId === undefined) return null;
mutations.note: Idempotence is the property a hook needs, because a hook fires whether or not the previous one already closed the run.

mutations.name: K3 drop the pending guard on the close
mutations.note: Closing on top of an uncertain frame publishes a second frame claiming a seq the pending one may already hold.

mutations.name: K4 drop the halted guard on the close
mutations.note: A halt means the stream's position is not known. The suite scripts a broker answer the mutant could use, so the kill is the guard and not an instrument running dry. RE-ANCHORED ON CODE when `closeRun` grew its `error` parameter: the old anchor embedded the one-line signature, which the new parameter list broke. The mutation is unchanged; only the text it hangs on moved.

mutations.name: K5 drop the onRunClosed report
mutations.note: Without the report a connector's mapper keeps attributing records to a run the published stream has already closed, and the emitter refuses the batch.

mutations.name: K6 the emitter ignores the failure it was handed and publishes a finish, which is the state this plane shipped in
mutations.note: The pre-fix behaviour exactly: every close is a RUN_FINISHED, so a failed turn is published as one that ended and a reader cannot tell it from one that succeeded.

mutations.name: K7 the holder drops the reason on the way to the emitter, so a reported failure closes as a finish
mutations.find: const runId = await emitter.closeRun({ timestamp, ...(error ? { error } : {}) });
mutations.note: A silent drop one layer above the emitter. The connector still believes it reported a failure, the emitter never hears about it, and the wire says the turn finished.

mutations.name: K8 skip the close-path bound so an oversized failure detail still throws in packUnits
mutations.note: Restores the defect: unbounded upstream text is packed as-is, packUnits refuses before beginSend, no terminal, holder dies.

mutations.name: K9 delete this.run = undefined from the shared terminal arm of AguiBrackets.accept
mutations.note: The machine stays open after RUN_ERROR, so a following ordinary close publishes RUN_FINISHED. The property was always this assignment; the ledger had claimed no such line existed.
